name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: Not a minor -- must have completed the age of twenty-one years.
12 months' continuous residence in Bangladesh immediately preceding the application.
requirements.fix_path: Remain continuously resident in Bangladesh for the 12 months immediately before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: At least 4 years' aggregate residence within the 7 years immediately preceding that final 12-month period.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 4 years of residence within the 7 years preceding the final qualifying year.

requirements.blocker_text: Good character, and intends to reside in Bangladesh or serve the Republic.

evidence_required.document: Renunciation of foreign citizenship (or evidence it will follow)

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: 12 months immediately preceding, plus at least 4 years' aggregate residence within the preceding 7 years

sources.title: UNHCR Refworld -- Naturalization Act, 1926 (as applied in Bangladesh via the Citizenship Act, 1951's certificate-of-naturalisation mechanism), Section 3(1): residence requirements (12 months immediately preceding + at least 4 of the preceding 7 years), age 21+ (not a minor), good character, adequate Bengali knowledge, intent to reside/serve; a special exemption from residence requirements applies to women who were citizens before marrying a non-citizen, if subsequently widowed or divorced

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bangladesh). STATUS: DRAFT -- the only source located for the exact numeric naturalisation criteria is UNHCR Refworld's hosted text of the colonial-era Naturalization Act, 1926, tier-2 under this dataset's convention. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the Citizenship Act, 1951 (Bangladesh's own post-independence citizenship statute) does NOT itself specify residence duration, age, or language requirements for naturalisation -- it instead operates by reference to a person having 'been granted a certificate of naturalisation under the Naturalisation Act, 1926', meaning the actual numeric criteria applicants must meet still derive from this 95-year-old British Indian colonial statute, not from any post-1971 Bangladeshi legislation. No tier-1 Bangladeshi-government-hosted copy of either Act's operative text was located in this build (bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd, the official Bangladesh laws portal, was unreachable at fetch time in this build -- worth a follow-up direct attempt). dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE per the Citizenship Act 1951's general prohibition (a citizen who is simultaneously a citizen of another country ceases to be a Bangladeshi citizen unless renouncing the foreign status, with an exception for persons under 21) -- this is the general rule that bd_citizenship_dual_nationality.json's Dual Nationality Certificate mechanism specifically carves an exception into for Bangladeshi-origin diaspora.
